title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: price increase
drivers.evidence: Sales dropped to x0.54 vs baseline at same price in 2026-09-28; recent week (2026-10-05) at $6.56 sold at x1.19, but below seasonal norm. Price increase of 2.3% likely suppresses demand, with historical sensitivity observed.

drivers.name: supply risk
drivers.evidence: Supplier warning of short delivery. While not confirmed, this may reduce available stock and dampen sales, especially if store limits quantities.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 44.5. No events or promotions in target week. Price increased 2.3% to $6.56. Recent weeks show a dip in sales at the higher price: 2026-09-28 (24 units, x0.54 vs baseline) and 2026-10-05 (53 units, x1.19). This suggests price sensitivity. Past promotions had median lift x1.57, but noise-adjusted x1.25; however, this is a price increase, not a discount. Post-promotion weeks show demand drop (x0.72, noise-adjusted x0.83). Supplier delivery warning adds supply risk, lowering confidence. No strong evidence for demand lift. Adjust down for price and supply risk.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.5 | 5%-95%: 15.7 - 71.7 | 10%-90%: 23.4 - 67.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
